note: Step 1's curation with the Registerinformation (and Unika) rows reversed, so B (2021) is the variant's first row. Row order inside a source reaches the build: prepare keeps the delivered order and convert_column_entry anchors an undated declaration on `records[0]`. Every projection is step 1's except the anchor ref, which moves to B's row: register 1, variant 2, edition 2021, variable 6, member 21. This pins today's row-order dependence, not an intended contract: an [[acknowledge]] pinned to that issue's evidence goes stale when a delivery is only re-sorted. Raised with the maintainer on the PR; if the anchor is made order-free, this step's ref flips to step 1's.
fails_if: `scb_errata.convert_column_entry` anchors an undated declaration on a record chosen independently of row order (for example the least ref), so the reversed rows keep step 1's anchor; or a step 1 claim breaks under reversed rows (the undated column gains a state, or pool loses its one pooled range)

sources.description: Step 1's rows reversed: variable 6 delivers B in 2021 (CVID 21), then variable 5 delivers A in 2020 (CVID 20).
